The reminder fired on `git commit -m"add export handler"` because the check read the message text as flags, and I've fixed and committed that as `97f1818`.

**Cause:** `shlex` turns `-m"add export handler"` into one word, `-madd export handler`. The cluster check looked for an `a` anywhere after the dash, so the `a` in "add" was taken for `-a` (stage everything). Any commit message containing an `a` triggered it, for example `-m"stage it"`.

**Fix** (`src/staging.py`): a short-option cluster is now read one letter at a time and stops at the first letter that takes a value (`C c F m t u` for `commit`). Whatever follows is the value, not more flags. Stage-all letters that come before a value letter are still caught, such as `-sam x` and `-am x`.

**Tests** (`tests/test_staging.py`): added cases for message text not being read as flags (`-m"add export handler"`, `-madd`, `-mA`, `-Fa`, `-ma "msg"`) and for stage-all still being caught when it follows a message flag. All 7 tests pass.

**Commit:** only `src/staging.py` and `tests/test_staging.py` went in. I left your uncommitted `README.md` note and the `notes/` folder alone. The commit message ends with the Co-Authored-By line from the reminder.

I couldn't read your user-level `~/.claude/settings.json`, so I didn't confirm which hook runs this check. The bug is in the repo's `src/staging.py`, which is what the tests cover.
